name: fine-pixel-cartoon

actual_tool_input.prompt:
Create ONE entirely new wide 16:9 in-game gameplay concept screenshot for Dias Irae. ONLY DRAWN TWO-DIMENSIONAL ART. No 3D art, 3D rendering, sculpted figures, 2.5D modeled surfaces, miniature photography, studio light, bevels or polished material gradients. This is a fully drawn game world, not a character portrait on a landscape backdrop.

CAMERA AND COMPOSITION: elevated orthographic three-quarter game camera at approximately 45 degrees above the horizontal ground, no horizon, no low cinematic viewpoint. Look DOWN into the scene; visible roof surfaces, helmet crown and feet positions must all agree. The playable hero is near the lower middle, roughly 9 percent of frame height INCLUDING his giant helmet, surrounded by traversable space. All people share the same game scale and elevated projection. An open diagonal muddy path leads toward the church in the upper left, a well is near the middle right, a burnt mill beside a stream sits at upper right. Two afflicted neighbors and one lean wolf occupy the path ahead as a readable small encounter. Use grounded contact marks but never rounded material modeling. Keep terrain readable as a playable surface and scenery visually separated from actors.

STORY: fictional Rivoire, in the Royans/Isere setting of southeastern France, late summer 1101. Poor small rural settlement: low limestone and timber houses, rough grey roofing, a modest Romanesque parish church with thick walls and round arches, exhausted rye plots blackened by blight, muddy well, shattered burnt watermill with a clotted wheel by a narrow stream. The church is small, no cathedral, no Gothic pointed arches, no later plate armor, no exotic non-European costume. Afflicted parishioners remain recognizable ordinary rural neighbors in worn tunics and hose, fearful and gaunt, not generic armored zombies or late-act demons. No high fantasy spires or magical glowing forest.

FIXED GUARIN COSTUME AND PROPORTIONS: extremely short, broad, squat and endearing cartoon knight. Huge full-face cylindrical iron greathelm with narrow black eye slit and a few small breathing holes, no exposed eyes or skin inside the helmet. Entire figure is only TWO helmet-heights tall; the helmet itself is almost half the total character height. Tiny broad torso, stubby short limbs and oversized little boots. Worn ring mail, torn faded wine-red scarf/cape and short waistcloth, plain brown leather gloves and belt, dirty brown leg wraps and short brown boots. One straight dull steel sword, straight blade and simple crossguard, in his right hand; taupe wooden kite shield with a single narrow faded wine-red vertical panel in his left. Keep these items consistent, no different outfits or realistic human proportions. The greathelm is an explicit permitted anachronism in the story, not a reason to move the village into a later century.

MOOD: dark, muddy, dirty, poor, worn, tired, desperate, dreary and hopeless. Characters are cute by their exaggerated structure, never cheerful or bright. Palette charcoal, peat brown, dirty limestone, dull iron and exhausted muted wine. Restrained contrast keeps the little player readable; no saturated red or blue scenery, no theatrical glow, no beautiful sunbeams. Hollow Knight informs silhouette economy and dark negative space; Diablo II informs oppressive village composition and grime rather than anatomically realistic figures. Light Castle Crashers influence only in squat structure. Apply the specific rendering style below to EVERYTHING in the scene, not just the hero.

A small restrained flat dark bottom interface strip may show one muted wine resource shape, one grey-blue resource shape, and four empty square action slots. No labels, numbers, logos, menus, watermark or dense text. Most of the frame is the game world. Do not add title art, panels, comparison sheets or portrait inserts.

SPECIFIC RENDERING STYLE FOR THIS ONE SCREEN:
Fine-resolution pixel cartoon: clear stepped black-brown contours and compact pixel clusters; rounded, simple, endearing oversized-head tiny-body silhouettes. Flat restrained color groups with occasional tiny checker dithering on rough cloth or stone. Tiny muted highlights only, no shiny gradients. Strong shape separation and more simplified surfaces than the other painted looks. Every building, enemy and hero is drawn as fine pixel game art, never a vector drawing or a 3D render. The structural sweetness of Hollow Knight and a light Castle Crashers influence, but the filthy muted grounded palette and hopeless rural mood of Diablo II. Keep the enclosed cylindrical helmet from the fixed costume: no visible face, hair, beard or big eyes even though the cartoon proportions are cute.

prompt_verification: Identical text; only the final newline was omitted by the dispatcher. No reference input.

visual_assessment.observations: Fine stepped pixel edges, simplified faces and compact color clusters translate the S01 rendering into a game scene. The later full-face greathelm rule replaces S01’s open face while retaining the cute cartoon medium.
visual_assessment.limitations: Legs are too long for the two-helmet-height target, the shield stripe is broad, and the mill contains an extra wheel. The detailed interface is provisional, not a game-system decision.

presentation: Presented for user review; not production approved
